questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Curl of a Vector Field
questions.problem: Consider the vector field $F={e}^{y+z}\,i+j+xyz\,k.$ Evaluate $∇\times F$ at the point  $(2,1,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the curl of $F$ is the vector field given by

$$
curl\,F=∇\times F=|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ P & Q & R\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {e}^{y+z} & 1 & xyz\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(1)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xyz)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{y+z})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(1)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y+z})]k \\  & =(xz-0)i-(yz-{e}^{y+z})j+(0-{e}^{y+z})k \\  & =xz\,i+({e}^{y+z}-yz)j-{e}^{y+z}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{curl}\,F$ at the point $(2,1,-1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\text{curl}\,F)(2,1,-1) & =2(-1)\,i+({e}^{1+(-1)}-1(-1))j-{e}^{1+(-1)}\,k \\  & =-2\,i+2\,j-k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the vector field $F=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,i+y{z}^{2}\,j+(x-z)\,k.$ Evaluate $∇\times F$ at the point  $(2,-1,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the curl of $F$ is the vector field given by

$$
curl\,F=∇\times F=|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ P & Q & R\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y) & y{z}^{2} & (x-z)\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-z)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(y{z}^{2})]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-z)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))]k \\  & =(0-2yz)i-(1-0)j+(0-\frac{1}{x+y})k \\  & =-2yz\,i-j-\frac{1}{x+y}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{curl}\,F$ at the point $(2,-1,3),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\text{curl}\,F)(2,-1,3) & =-2(-1)(3)\,i-j-\frac{1}{2+(-1)}\,k \\  & =6\,i-j-k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the vector field $F={x}^{2}\,i+xz\,j+{z}^{2}\,k.$ Evaluate $∇\times F$ at the point  $(-2,-3,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the curl of $F$ is the vector field given by

$$
curl\,F=∇\times F=|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ P & Q & R\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {x}^{2} & xz & {z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2})]k \\  & =(0-x)i-(0-0)j+(z-0)k \\  & =-x\,i+z\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{curl}\,F$ at the point $(-2,-3,1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\text{curl}\,F)(-2,-3,1) & =-(-2)\,i+(1)\,k \\  & =2\,i+\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Scalar Curl of a Vector Field
questions.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=(2x+{y}^{2})\,i+y{e}^{x}\,j.$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{x})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x+{y}^{2}) \\  & =y{e}^{x}-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(1,1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(1,1)} & =(1){e}^{1}-2(1) \\  & =e-2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,i+(x{y}^{2}+1)\,j.$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(0,\frac{\pi }{2}).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}+1)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)) \\  & ={y}^{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(0,\frac{\pi }{2}),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(0,\pi /2)} & ={(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0+\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}-0 \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14045767/assets/4c38294780ac6d5079b759f39a7dbd4944b1c3c21495245dfd314ec180c0434e.png)

Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z),$ shown above. Given that $F(x,y,z)$ is independent of $z,$ which of the following statements are true?

- $\text{curl}\,F=0$
- $\text{curl}\,F\ne 0$
- $F$ is irrotational
- $\text{curl}\,F$ points in the positive $z$-direction.
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{curl}\,F$ denotes the curl of the vector field $F.$

To understand intuitively whether a vector field has curl at a point $P$, imagine that our vector field $F$ represents the velocity field of a stream of flowing water. We place a paddlewheel at $P$ with the axis of rotation pointing in the $z$-direction, and we note whether the paddlewheel rotates or not.

- If the paddlewheel does not rotate due to the action of the water, then the velocity field has zero curl, i.e., $\text{curl}\,F=0.$

- If the paddlewheel is forced to rotate due to the action of the water, then the vector field has curl, i.e., $\text{curl}\,F\ne 0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14045767/assets/979b63f21e56924bd7880f9487cf829089e38cf14d287e70196c7a661e41f97f.png)

Moreover, if $\text{curl}\,F=0$ everywhere in ${R}^{3}$, we say that $F$ is irrotational.

With that in mind, let's check each statement:

- Statement I is true, whereas statement II is false. If a paddlewheel were placed at any point $P$ in the manner described above, it would not rotate. Therefore, $\text{curl}\,F=0.$

- Statement III is true. Since $\text{curl}\,F=0,$ the vector field $F$ is irrotational.

- Statement IV is false. Since $\text{curl}\,F=0,$ it points in neither the positive nor the negative $z$-direction.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

canonical_examples.problem: Consider the vector field $\mathbf{F} = y\,\mathbf{i} + x^2\,\mathbf{j} - 2z\,\mathbf{k}.$ Evaluate $\textrm{curl}\,\mathbf{F}$ at the point  $\left(-1,0,2\right).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf{F}=P\,\mathbf{i}+Q\,\mathbf{j}+R\,\mathbf{k}$ is a vector field on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $\mathbf F$ all exist, then the curl of $\mathbf F$ is the vector field given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14045767/assets/888b12c4f687dba1199a82d7e3a5e6897e7599ea812753423de5a23ffd756888.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ y & {x}^{2} & -2z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2z)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2})]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2z)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(y)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(y)]k \\  & =(0-0)i-(0-0)j+(2x-1)k \\  & =(2x-1)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\textrm {curl}\, \mathbf{F}$ at the point $\left(-1,0,2\right),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(\text{curl}\,F)(-1,0,2) & =(2(-1)-1)\,k=-3\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Consider the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y) = e^{x+y} \, \mathbf{i} + 3xy \, \mathbf{j}.$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $\mathbf{F}$ at the point $(-1,1).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf{F} = P\,\mathbf{i} + Q\,\mathbf{j}$ is a vector field on $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $\mathbf F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $\mathbf{F}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x+y}) \\  & =3y-{e}^{x+y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(-1,1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(-1,1)} & =3(1)-{e}^{-1+1} \\  & =3-{e}^{0} \\  & =3-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14045767/assets/71c58bf1b0fe4259ac50633a457f6a76639c0a0c188b66cce5e0fc3c7e5b0329.png)

 

Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z),$ shown above. Given that $\mathbf F(x,y,z)$ is independent of $z,$ which of the following statements are true?

- $\textrm{curl}\,\mathbf F = \mathbf 0$

- $\textrm{curl}\, \mathbf F \neq \mathbf 0$

- $\mathbf F$ is irrotational

- $\textrm{curl}\, \mathbf F$ points in the positive $z$-direction.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall that $\textrm{curl}\,\mathbf F$ denotes the curl of the vector field $\mathbf F.$

To understand intuitively whether a vector field has curl at a point $P$, imagine that our vector field $\mathbf F$ represents the velocity field of a stream of flowing water. We place a paddlewheel at $P$ with the axis of rotation pointing in the $z$-direction, and we note whether the paddlewheel rotates or not.

- If the paddlewheel is forced to rotate due to the action of the water, then the vector field has curl, i.e., $\textrm{curl}\,\mathbf F \neq  \mathbf 0.$

- If the paddlewheel does not rotate due to the action of the water, then the velocity field has zero curl, i.e., $\textrm{curl}\,\mathbf F =  \mathbf 0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14045767/assets/86aee33cdfa96ac0a61468cc9657e791e399f31c024cdbc3a932193dc897d534.png)

If $\textrm{curl}\,\mathbf F = \mathbf 0$ everywhere in $\mathbb R^3$, we say that $\mathbf F$ is irrotational.

With that in mind, let's check each statement:

- Statement I is false, whereas statement II is true. If a paddlewheel were placed at any point $P$ in the manner described above, it would rotate counterclockwise. Therefore, $\textrm{curl}\,\mathbf F \neq \mathbf 0.$

- Statements III is false. Since $\textrm{curl}\,\mathbf F \neq \mathbf 0,$ the vector field $\mathbf F$ is not irrotational.

- Statement IV is true. Using our right hand, if we wrap our fingers in the direction of rotation (counterclockwise), our thumb will point upward. Therefore, $\textrm{curl}\,\mathbf F$ points upward, in the direction of increasing $z.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and IV only."
